mechanism_narrative: The sustained high level of residential mobility indicates that a significant portion of the population continues to stay home, directly reducing the need and opportunity for retail and recreation outings, leading to lower RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days, despite RESIDENTIAL mobility remaining above 20%.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES mobility remains consistently below -50% for the next two weeks, it signifies a continued widespread remote work policy, which will suppress weekday retail and recreation activity, resulting in lower RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES remains below -50% for 2 consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days increases by more than 5 points, even if WORKPLACES mobility stays below -50%.

mechanism_narrative: A slight week-on-week increase in GROCERY_PHARM mobility combined with a simultaneous week-on-week decrease in RESIDENTIAL mobility suggests a cautious return to essential out-of-home activities, which will marginally spill over to RETAIL_REC, leading to a slight increase over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises and RESIDENTIAL falls week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days decreases, despite GROCERY_PHARM rising and RESIDENTIAL falling week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: The persistently low transit station mobility, hovering around -70%, indicates ongoing public health directives or strong public apprehension regarding shared transportation, which will continue to deter non-essential travel and depress RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days shows an increase of more than 10 points, while TRANSIT mobility remains below -65%.

mechanism_narrative: If PARKS mobility continues its recent downward trend, falling below -35% in the next week, it signals a broader reduction in outdoor and leisure activities, which will negatively impact RETAIL_REC over the next week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls below -35% in the next week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days increases, despite PARKS mobility falling below -35%.

mechanism_narrative: The current deeply negative and stable RETAIL_REC mobility (-70% range) reflects entrenched consumer habits such as increased online shopping and reduced discretionary spending, which will persist and keep RETAIL_REC low over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days increases by more than 10 points from its current average, indicating a shift in consumer behavior.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in WORKPLACES mobility by at least 5 points and a decrease in RESIDENTIAL mobility by at least 2 points over the next two weeks would indicate a gradual return to office-based work, stimulating a modest increase in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises by >5 points and RESIDENTIAL falls by >2 points over 2 weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days decreases, despite WORKPLACES rising by >5 points and RESIDENTIAL falling by >2 points over 2 weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The combined sustained low levels of TRANSIT and WORKPLACES mobility suggest that official guidance or policies discouraging commuting and encouraging remote work are still strongly in effect, which will continue to suppress RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days increases by more than 5 points, even with both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remaining below -50%.
